gap.title: Open, a hard one: do linear spaces on which the permanent near the all-ones matrix stays constant have dimension at most a constant times n? It may be false
gap.statement: ∃ C : ℕ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (L : Submodule ℂ (Fin n × Fin n → ℂ)), (∀ t ∈ L, MvPolynomial.eval (fun p => 1 + t p) (PEqualNP.Gct.permPoly ℂ n) = (Nat.factorial n : ℂ)) → Module.finrank ℂ L ≤ C * n
gap.unlocks: With the checked reduction L-gct-077 it gives border size m^2 - O(m) for the permanent
gap.context: OPEN: A HARD ONE. Checked so far: a space of dimension 2n - 3 exists (L-gct-080); the problem reduces to doubly centred spaces (L-gct-092); the 3 by 3 case (L-gct-094); product-type parts are bounded (L-gct-090). A proof must use Taylor orders growing with n. A proof must prove exactly the recorded statement, with no sorry, no new axiom and no native_decide. Put every declaration of your file inside its own namespace.
